title: The Amazing harvest that year
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：amazing　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 amazing 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the observer wrote of ① an amazing harvest that year in the log, and everybody in the observatory said at once that it was ② more amazing than the one named there the year before. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the observer, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the amazing ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most amazing harvest that year anybody in the observatory had ever seen, or so the log for November 1951 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too amazing to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the assistant who had come to help; the amazing ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the lens at the far dome, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ an amazing act of kindness, and said that no assistant in his right mind would call it ⑥ as amazing as the act of kindness they had once had in the old observatory. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was amazing or not, and he said so.

By 1964 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the log. What the line asked for was ⑦ something amazing, and nothing besides. The assistant from the next observatory called the whole plan ⑧ quite amazing; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the log kept the names of the amazing ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1967, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another amazing harvest that year in the same log, and the work, which took two nights, seemed  more amazing than anybody had expected.  The most amazing act of kindness in the whole observatory, she said in 1969, was the one she could never quite name; the amazing ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 惊人（前置定语 an amazing harvest that year：1957 年观测员在观测记录里记下的那件惊人的收成）
B. adj. 惊人／了不起（比较级 more amazing than：文中两处，一处比那年的收成，一处比预想）
C. adj. 惊人／了不起（最高级 the most amazing：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 惊人（表语 too amazing to do：母亲觉得它太惊人，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 了不起（前置定语 an amazing act of kindness：叔叔把整件事称作一桩了不起的善举）
F. adj. 了不起（同级比较 as amazing as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩善举相比）
G. adj. 了不起（后置定语 something amazing：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 了不起（受程度副词修饰 quite amazing：那位助手的评价）

items.q: the most amazing harvest that year anybody

answers.why: amazing 意为“惊人”，1957 年观测员在观测记录里记下的是“一件惊人的收成”，此处作前置定语 an amazing harvest that year。
amazing 意为“惊人”，此处用比较级 more amazing than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
amazing 意为“惊人”，观测记录上 十一月 那行字说它是观测站里最惊人的一件，故用最高级 the most amazing harvest that year。
amazing 意为“惊人”，母亲认为这件东西“太惊人了，谁也用不上”，too amazing to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
amazing 意为“了不起”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩了不起的善举”，此处作前置定语 an amazing act of kindness。
amazing 意为“了不起”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩善举一样了不起”，同级比较用 as amazing as。
amazing 意为“了不起”，观测记录上那半行字要的是“了不起的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something amazing。
amazing 意为“了不起”，邻观测站来的那位助手认为这套计划“相当了不起”，quite 修饰原级 amazing。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1957 年，观测员在观测记录里记下了一件惊人的收成。（an amazing harvest that year）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更惊人。（more amazing than …）
母亲觉得它太惊人，谁也用不上。（too amazing to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩了不起的善举。（an amazing act of kindness）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩善举一样了不起。（as amazing as …）
到了 1964 年，观测记录上只剩半行字：要的是一件了不起的东西。（something amazing）
answers: In 1957 the observer wrote of an amazing harvest that year in the log.
Everybody said it was more amazing than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too amazing to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business an amazing act of kindness.
He said nobody would call it as amazing as the act of kindness they had once had.
By 1964 the log asked for nothing but something amazing.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 amazing 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1957 the observer wrote of an amazing harvest that year in the log, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most amazing harvest that year in the observatory, or so the log says.
My mother thought it too amazing to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business an amazing act of kindness, and nobody argued with him.
The assistant from the next observatory called the plan quite amazing, and everybody laughed.
The amazing ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
